items.ig_caption:
Chase. Visa. Mastercard. Three vendor incidents in one week. 🏦

What The Next Web reported (19 Nov):
→ JPMorgan Chase says third parties that provide services to it were the target of a cyber attack
→ Attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses
→ Visa confirmed an incident at a third-party provider: "Visa's systems were not involved" and no card numbers were affected
→ Mastercard says an outside provider exposed a limited number of emails from one benefit programme, now contained
→ A group calling itself n0n claims the leak; the companies have not named the vendors

My take: Your vendor's marketing database is your breach too. I'd list every vendor holding customer emails, and warn customers now that a phish using their real name is coming.

What to do: if you're a customer, treat any call or email about this breach as suspect and contact your bank through its official number. If you run security, ask which vendors hold your customer data and how fast they'd tell you.

items.ig_caption:
Exploited for more than two months before a patch existed. ⚠️

What SecurityWeek reported (19 Nov):
→ CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS 9.8) in VMware vCenter lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker get an admin session
→ Google says a China-linked espionage group exploited it for more than two months before the patch
→ Mandiant links it to Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221); initial access came via a BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day
→ Per Mandiant, the attackers stole SAML signing material, created an SSO admin, forged tokens and moved to ESXi
→ Broadcom's fixes: vCenter 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200 and 8.0 U3m; no public patch for out-of-support 7.0

My take: Patching isn't enough when it was a zero-day for months. I'd patch, then hunt: new SSO admins, SAML signing changes, odd ESXi logins. 7.0 still running? That's the priority.

What to do: patch now, then look for evidence of compromise, as Mandiant's CTO advises. Start with new SSO admin accounts and unusual ESXi access.
